glossary_intro: The terms, symbols, and printing details on Riftbound cards and across OpenRift. Entries link to the comprehensive rules.
glossary_domains_intro: Riftbound has six domains, each with its own colour and symbol: Fury, Calm, Mind, Body, Chaos, and Order. A card's domain is shown by glyphs in the lower-right corner of the card, and runes of that domain produce the Power needed to pay its costs. Your Champion Legend's domains determine your deck's Domain Identity, which limits which other cards you can include.
glossary_card_types_intro: A card's type tells you how and where it interacts with the game. Units fight on battlefields, Gear attaches to a Unit you control, Spells resolve their effects and leave play, Runes sit in your Rune Pool to produce Energy and Power, Battlefields are the locations Units fight over, and Legends sit beside your deck and represent your Champion.
glossary_supertypes_intro: Supertypes apply on top of a card's type and are listed before it on the card face. They mostly affect deckbuilding.
glossary_supertype_champion_description: Applies exclusively to Units. Determines who can be your Chosen Champion.
glossary_supertype_signature_description: Can apply to any card type. Limited to 3 per deck, tied to your Champion's tag.
glossary_supertype_token_description: Temporary game objects created by effects, not part of a deck.
glossary_keywords_intro: Keywords are short words or phrases that stand in for a longer rule. They appear in card text in square brackets, like [Equip] or [Deathknell]. Tap a rule reference to jump to the full definition.
glossary_symbols_intro: Riftbound uses a small set of inline symbols on cards to express costs and core game concepts compactly.
glossary_symbol_might_summary: A unit's combat power. Higher Might deals more damage and is harder to remove.
glossary_symbol_might_bonus_summary: A boxed Might value on Gear, indicating how much Might the gear adds to its equipped unit.
glossary_symbol_exhaust_summary: Turning a card, rune, or legend sideways to use it. Once exhausted, it can't be exhausted again until something readies it.
glossary_symbol_recycle_summary: Place a card or rune from the board onto the bottom of its deck. Often used to pay Power costs.
glossary_symbol_power_activation_summary: Exhaust a rune of a specific domain to add its Power to your Rune Pool, then spend it to pay costs.
glossary_symbol_energy_summary: Pay Energy by exhausting any rune, regardless of domain. Shown as a numeric cost on the card.
glossary_symbol_rune_rainbow_summary: Marked [A]. A Power cost that can be paid with a rune of any domain. This is the wild Power symbol.
glossary_rarities_intro: Every printing has a rarity, shown by the coloured glyph in the middle of the card face. Rarity reflects how often a card appears in booster packs and the visual treatment of its frame, not its strength in play. The Showcase tier is reserved for premium full-art and alternative-art printings.
glossary_booster_intro_before: A standard Riftbound booster contains 14 cards across five slot types. The
glossary_booster_rates_note: Headline rates come from Riot's Origins announcement. Foil-slot and cascade rates are community estimates.
glossary_pack_slot_rare_description: Each flex slot rolls Epic about 13.4% of the time and Rare otherwise, which works out to roughly 1 in 4 packs containing at least one Epic.
glossary_pack_slot_foil_description: Usually a Common (~70%) or Uncommon (~25%) foil, occasionally upgrading to a Rare (~4%) or Epic (~1%) foil. The whole slot can be replaced by a Showcase alt-art (~1 per 12 packs), an overnumbered Showcase (1 per 72 packs), a signed Showcase (1 per 720 packs), or an Ultimate (~0.1% of packs, where the pool has one).
glossary_pack_slot_rune_description: Usually a basic Rune. Occasionally a foil Rune, sometimes a Token-supertype card (e.g. Sprite, Recruit), and very rarely an alt-art Rune.
glossary_art_variants_intro: An art variant describes which illustration appears on a printing. Alt-art printings are usually marked by a lowercase letter suffix on the card number, like OGN-120a.
glossary_art_variant_altart: An additional artwork using the same card name and rarity. Distinguished by a lowercase letter suffix on the card number (e.g. 120a).
glossary_art_variant_overnumbered: Reprinted art with a card number that exceeds the printed set total, typically a special variant slotted into a later set.
glossary_art_variant_ultimate: A premium full-art treatment. The card itself usually keeps its original rarity (e.g. Showcase), since Ultimate describes the artwork, not the rarity.
glossary_finishes_intro: Finish describes the physical production treatment of a printing. Most cards use a normal cardstock finish, foil printings add a glossy reflective coating across the card face, and a small number have been released as premium metal collectibles. Finish is independent of rarity and art variant, so the same artwork can exist as both a normal and a foil printing.
glossary_finish_normal: Standard cardstock with no special treatment.
glossary_finish_foil: Glossy foil finish across the card face.
glossary_finish_metal_deluxe: Higher-tier metal printing with extra finishing.
glossary_markers_intro: Markers describe how a printing was distributed rather than what's on the card. They cover promotional channels like prereleases, tournaments, judge programs, and store-level events, and a single printing can carry more than one.
glossary_printing_details_intro: Artist credit is tracked per printing so reprints can preserve the original illustrator, and the signature flag marks printings where the artist's signature is overlaid on the artwork (usually on a foil alt-art or Ultimate variant).
glossary_printing_detail_artist_descript: Illustrator credit printed on the card. Tracked per printing so reprints can credit the original artist.
glossary_printing_detail_signature_descr: A printing flag indicating the card carries the artist's signature, usually overlaid on a foil alt-art or Ultimate variant.
glossary_sets_intro_before: Sets are how Riftbound releases new cards. Each set has a three-letter code that prefixes every card number in it, and is classified as either a main set (the regular release cadence) or a supplemental set (smaller drops outside the main schedule). Browse the full catalogue of any set on the
glossary_numbering_intro: Every printing has a short code combining the three-letter set code with a card number, like OGN-007.
glossary_numbering_base: Set code followed by the printed card number.
glossary_numbering_altart: A lowercase letter suffix marks an alt-art variant of the same base card. Distinct from the Showcase rarity, which is shown by the rarity glyph in the middle of the card.
glossary_numbering_overnumbered: A number above the set's printed total is an Overnumbered variant, usually a special reprint slotted into a later set.
glossary_numbering_token: T prefix indicates a token printed for the set. T and R prefixes were introduced with Spiritforged. Origins used standard numbering for tokens and runes.
glossary_numbering_rune: R prefix indicates a rune printed for the set (introduced in Spiritforged).
